## Day 1 Flashcards

Press **q** to flip a card, **t** to shuffle and jump to the first card, or use the arrow keys / flip button to navigate.

::: footer
Based on [Day 1 notes](day1.qmd).
:::

## {background-color="#eef6ff"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
Per Joe Cheng's opening quote, what is "winning" the battle between convenience and correctness?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
Convenience.

> In the battle between convenience and correctness, convenience is winning.
:::

## {background-color="#eef6ff"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What is "approval fatigue," and why does it undercut the "just add a human reviewer" fix?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
People stop reading agent requests and just click approve — so a human-in-the-loop checkpoint doesn't reliably catch mistakes; the *system* needs to be designed for correctness instead.
:::

## {background-color="#eef6ff"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What does {commons} do, and what do its three response markers (🟢 🔵 🟡) mean?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
It routes agent questions through **trusted code** the team already relies on instead of always generating bespoke code.

🟢 trusted calculation · 🔵 cited trusted context · 🟡 freehand code (no trust anchor)
:::

## {background-color="#fff7e6"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
Define **harness**, **tool**, and **agent** per Keyes's talk.
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
**harness** — a program that coordinates calls to an LLM and other software systems

**tool** — a function the LLM can ask the harness to run on its behalf

**agent** — an LLM within a harness using tools iteratively in a loop until it accomplishes a task
:::

## {background-color="#fff7e6"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
In the patient-chart-summarizer eval, which harness pattern was both the best quality *and* the cheapest — and why?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
The **agent** harness — because it chooses which notes to read via tools instead of re-reading every note every time (unlike the workflow harness).
:::

## {background-color="#eef6ff"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
In the NYC Squirrel Count persona study, which persona preserved the most data with the fewest destructive changes, and which discarded the most?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
**Data manager** — preserved most, fewest destructive changes.

**Environmental researcher** — dropped the most data, made the most assumptions.
:::

## {background-color="#eef6ff"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What are the three "pause, ask, follow directions" skill design rules?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
1. Only pause on decisions that change the question/method/story/interpretation
2. Give just enough context to decide
3. Never editorialize ("great choice," "are you sure?") — present options and follow the user's direction
:::

## {background-color="#fff7e6"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What did Brittany (Posit's finance team) build, and what did it save her?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
Claude skills to draft finance entries and parse bills, as a non-engineer — saved 5–10 hrs/week, with no sensitive data sent to Anthropic.
:::

## {background-color="#fff7e6"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What point did the "counting 'n's in unconventional" exercise make?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
Asking an LLM directly for a letter count fails, but asking it to *write code* that counts succeeds — because tokens aren't the same thing as letters.
:::

## {background-color="#eef6ff"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What was Cashorali's closing message, and in what order?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
Talk to humans first → agree on what words mean → make sure it's a question worth answering.

> If you don't talk to humans first, AI is a great way to automate misunderstandings.
:::

## {background-color="#eef6ff"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
Give one example of "tribal knowledge" that turned out to need an explicit definition in the pharma project.
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
"Called on" meant *any* interaction (call, email, Zoom, in-office) — not just phone calls. ("Active patient" and "recently" = 30 vs. 60 days were two more.)
:::

## {background-color="#fff7e6"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What's Sharon Wang's core reframe of "what context do agents need"?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
The durable question is "what context do *you* need" — you can't write down for an agent what you don't understand yourself.
:::

## {background-color="#fff7e6"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
Name two signs it's time to start a new chat instead of pushing through a degraded context window.
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
A new task, a side quest, or catching yourself re-explaining in circles.
:::

## {background-color="#eef6ff"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What's James Wade's reframe of "am I sacrificing capability by staying in R?"
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
Agents don't need the largest ecosystem, they need a *coherent* one — only switch languages when there's a compelling reason, not by default.
:::

## {background-color="#eef6ff"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What does {deputy} add on top of {ellmer}?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
Permissions and usage limits on top of ellmer's tool-calling classes — enterprise-style safety controls.
:::

## {background-color="#fff7e6"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What is the "lethal trifecta" (Simon Willison), cited in this talk?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
An agent combining (1) access to private data, (2) exposure to untrusted content, and (3) the ability to communicate out — can be tricked via prompt injection into exfiltrating private data.
:::

## {background-color="#fff7e6"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
When does a CLI beat a custom MCP server, per Richardson?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
When the CLI already exists, is widely used, and is already in the model's training data (e.g. `gh`) — no context spent teaching the model how to use it.
:::

## {background-color="#eef6ff"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
Why does total conversation cost grow roughly *quadratically*, not linearly, with conversation length?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
LLMs are stateless — every request resends the entire prior conversation, so total spend is the cumulative sum of every growing request.
:::

## {background-color="#eef6ff"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What's the single biggest cost lever Chang highlighted?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
Prompt caching — repeated input tokens (in the same order as an earlier request) are served from cache at roughly 1/10th the normal input-token cost.
:::

## {background-color="#fff7e6"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What are Wickham's two "profound but durable" principles for AI-human data science collaboration?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
> Write shit down. And then look at how shit has changed.

(data-dict = write it down; data-diff = look at how it changed)
:::

## {background-color="#fff7e6"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What does data-dict record, and how is it shipped?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
A YAML spec of column types/descriptions/examples, table joins, and a glossary of domain terms — shipped as a self-contained Rust CLI (no R/Python runtime needed).
:::

## {background-color="#eef6ff"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What's the layering of the Shiny AI stack, bottom to top?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
ellmer/chatlas (tidy LLM interface) → shinychat (chat UI toolkit) → domain-specific packages on top, like {commons} and querychat.
:::

## {background-color="#eef6ff"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What is querychat's deliberate capability restriction, and why?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
It restricts agent code execution to SQL/ggsql only — a safety/capability tradeoff that lets read-only DB permissions be enforced at the database layer.
:::

## {background-color="#fff7e6"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What is Positron **Canvas**?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
An early, non-IDE-centric agent surface prototype — collapsed tool calls, a dedicated artifacts pane for plots, and a "live Quarto report mode," built on the same engine as Posit Assistant.
:::

## {background-color="#fff7e6"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What is the **Trajectory reviewer** in Commons?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
It captures real post-deployment user conversations (with disclosure) so the team can see what questions actually came up, then feeds that back into a coding agent to add new measures/context — moving traffic up the trust ladder.
:::

## {background-color="#eef6ff"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What incident motivated Posit Team's new LLM spend-cap features?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
Posit's own team once burned $50,000 unexpectedly running Bedrock-backed deployments on Connect before anyone noticed.
:::

## {background-color="#eef6ff"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What's **destructive-command-guard**, and how does it fix the "agent did something I told it not to" problem?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
An open-source, deterministic pre-tool-call hook that blocks destructive git/package-manager commands before they run — free and fast since it needs no LLM (stronger prompting alone doesn't reliably work).
:::

## {background-color="#fff7e6"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
Why does the NYT publish a *uniformly* shaded margin-of-error band instead of the more statistically accurate bell-curve band?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
It's a deliberate compromise between statistical correctness and audience familiarity — many readers aren't used to reading a density/histogram shape.
:::

## {background-color="#fff7e6"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What is "non-response bias," and how is it different from sampling error?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
Bias from certain kinds of people being less likely to respond to a poll at all — unlike sampling error, it isn't calculable from a simple formula.
:::

## {background-color="#fff7e6"}

::: {.flashcard-front}
What is the NYT election-night "needle," and why did the Times *not* use it for the Michigan Senate primary?
:::

::: {.flashcard-back}
Two dials — a margin estimate with an uncertainty band, plus a second dial in words (toss-up / lean X / likely X). Withheld for the primary because polling was so unreliable (off by ~9 points) that the dial's confident-looking swings would have overstated certainty.
:::
